disposition_reason: Table 5 prints the range and median of lead, cadmium, zinc and copper in 24 polyfloral honeys from six apiaries around a historically polluted non-ferrous metal industrial site.

study.design: Case study of apiaries at increasing distance from an industrial pollution source
study.origin: Copsa Mica, Micasasa, Tarnava, Valea Viilor and Seica Mica, Sibiu area, Romania
study.market: collected directly from local beekeepers (stationary apiaries)
study.method: 1 g honey in water, HNO3 microwave digestion (Top Wave); Pb and Cd by GFAAS, Zn and Cu by flame AAS (Shimadzu AA-6300)
study.qa: Triplicate digestion and blank; no CRM or recovery reported

findings.group: six stationary apiaries, Copsa Mica and neighboring villages (1.1-10.5 km from the industrial platform)
findings.notes: Coefficient of variation 56.27%. Industrially polluted area; four samples per apiary.

controls.control: apiary exposure to the main valley air corridor
controls.comparator: frontal exposure (main valley) vs secondary valley apiaries
controls.outcome: Pb on average about 1 mg/kg higher in main-valley apiaries (Mann-Whitney p = 0.05); Cd, Zn, Cu not different

controls.comparator: apiaries 1.12 to 10.54 km from the source
controls.outcome: Cd decreases and Cu increases with distance (figure only, values not read); Pb and Zn unrelated (Spearman -0.029, p = 0.96)

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU maximum levels cited (Regulation 1881/2006 as amended by 2015/1005)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: Pb 0.10 mg/kg; Cd 0.05 mg/kg; median Pb exceeds the limit
